title: feat(desktop): workspaces part 1 — registry, migration, switch and switcher (NIW2-580)
body:
Linear: [NIW2-580](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-580) — part 1 of several workspaces ([NIW2-370](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-370)). Design: spec and ADR 0032 on [#431](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/431) (not merged yet); UI: Claude Design "Kaipu Workspaces v2", section 1.

## What this does

A workspace is a folder with Kaipu's files. One is active, and the Library, the editors, tags and every new capture use it.

- **Registry** in `userData/preferences.json`: a `workspaces` key with `entries` (`id`, `name`, `path`, `color`, `initials`, `addedAt`, optional `pendingInit`), `activeId`, `legacyCloudOwnerId` and `hintDismissedAt`. `vaultDirectory` keeps mirroring the active path on every switch, and is absent when that path is the default folder, so an older version opens the active library.
- **Migration** on the first launch: the current library (custom or default folder) becomes **"Default workspace"** (DW, `rose`) and gets `.kaipu/workspace/identity.json`. Nothing else changes. Media, sidecars, `tags.json` and `settings.json` stay byte-identical (tested by hash, including a customer's `workspace.png` and `settings.png` sidecars). It is idempotent. A crash between the two writes reuses the identity's id. A `preferences.json` that does not parse is never overwritten: the app runs read-only and retries next launch. An unreachable custom folder is registered `pendingInit` and initialized on first reach. A folder that an older version switched to is adopted on the next launch.
- **Add workspace** picks an existing folder. It writes only `.kaipu/workspace/identity.json`, or adopts the one it finds there. An id this Mac already knows at a reachable path is treated as a copy and gets a new id; at an unreachable path it is a relocation. A folder Kaipu cannot write into is refused and left as it was. **Remove from list** unregisters only and touches nothing on disk. It is refused for the active and the last workspace, and asks for confirmation.
- **Not connected**: a registered root is never recreated (`LibraryVault.list()` no longer `mkdir`s it, and finalize no longer `mkdir`s the vault). When the active workspace is missing, recordings, exports and screenshot saves are refused with "<name> isn't connected… Nothing was saved elsewhere". The bar and the Record and Library pages show the state.
- **Switch transaction** in main (`main/workspaces/switch-transaction.ts`):
  1. Refuse while a recording or export runs: the LOCKED state.
  2. Probe the target folder.
  3. Ask every window to prepare:
     - editors flush their pending save;
     - pages that hold an item navigate away, so the editors' existing leave guards ask about unsaved work (Keep editing cancels the switch);
     - the window then refuses item calls.
  4. Close the gate, which drains running calls.
  5. Dismiss the capture toast and drop the retained quiet-capture bytes.
  6. Persist `activeId` and `vaultDirectory`.
  7. Bump the generation, set the window title, and broadcast.
  
  The renderer remounts its routes on the new generation, so lists, filters and editors are rebuilt.
- **Stale calls**: every item-scoped and tag call goes through `WorkspaceGate.run(stamp, …)`. That covers list, rename, tags, delete, reveal, drag, edit session, screenshot read, copy and save, GIF save, and remove local copy. The preload attaches the window's `{workspaceId, generation}` stamp. Main rejects a stale stamp with `stale-workspace` and writes nothing. The preload also discards an answer that arrives after the stamp changed, and `reportError` stays silent for these.
- **Binding**: `RecordingWriter` resolves the folder once at `create()`. Finalize and the cursor track use that folder, so a take never splits. A quiet capture carries its workspace id into the retained bytes, the toast payload and the toast's Save, which writes only while that workspace is active. Thumbnail and screenshot URLs from `describe()` carry `?w=<id>`, and `kaipu-media://` refuses another workspace's id.
- **Copy**:
  - the window title is "<Workspace> — Kaipu Record" once a second workspace exists;
  - on Record, "Recording to <Workspace> · Switch" replaces "Ready to record";
  - the toast reads "Saved to <Workspace>", "Save to <Workspace>" and "Also saved to <Workspace>", as a label only;
  - Settings → Files becomes Settings → Workspaces, and `/settings/files` redirects there.
  
  en and es keys are added. `record.readyToRecord` stays, because the web landing still uses it.
- **Startup sweeps** (drag copies and stranded takes) run for every connected workspace, each into its own folder.

## Spec vs design deviations

Where the spec and the design disagree, the spec wins:

1. **Visible with one workspace.** The design hides the bar when only one workspace exists. Following the owner's decision (spec decision 19), the bar always shows, the menu offers "Add workspace…", and the one-time hint "New: workspaces — keep work and personal captures apart" sits under the bar. It is dismissed by its button, by Escape, or by adding a workspace, and is stored as `hintDismissedAt` in `preferences.json`.
2. **Placement.** The spec has rail tiles (decision 11); the design has a header row right of the rail. The owner has not chosen, so this follows the v2 design. `WorkspaceSwitcher` is self-contained and mounted once, in `shell/app-shell.tsx`; moving it is a one-line change. Rail tiles, the status-bar chip and ⌘digit switching are not built.
3. **Menu shortcuts.** Finder (Explorer on Windows) opens the folder. Settings navigates to the existing Settings → Workspaces page. Cloud is left out.
4. **Cloud label.** The design's bar label and the menu's "Cloud" stat describe per-workspace cloud, which is part 4. The bar shows where the folder lives instead ("This Mac" or the drive name), and the stat reads "Location".
5. **Window title.** The ticket asks for "<Workspace> — Kaipu Record". The spec's acceptance criteria keep the plain "Kaipu Record" until a second workspace exists, so that is what this does.

Also worth knowing:

- **Spec order of the transaction.** The spec drains the gate first and then asks windows to prepare. Done in that order, an editor's flush would be refused. This prepares first and drains second, which matches the ticket's order (flush → prompt → close → clear → bump).
- **Add switches.** After Add workspace, the app switches to the new workspace through the normal transaction. If the switch is refused, for example during a recording, the workspace stays registered and inactive.
- **Cloud entries without a workspace id** belong to `legacyCloudOwnerId` (spec decision 3). Another workspace shows only the cloud copies of its own local items and never rewrites the account's catalog cache. No entry has a workspace id yet: desktop upload has not shipped.
- **Media URLs** carry the workspace as `?w=<id>`, not as a path segment. URLs built by the renderer (playback) still resolve against the active workspace, and their pages are remounted on a switch.
- **Not in this part:**
  - the tray submenu (it is not trivial: the tray menu has no data path for it yet);
  - Rename, and a name field in the add dialog (new workspaces take their folder's name);
  - the "Saving to" labels on the capture panel and overlay, and the control-bar chip;
  - the Library header name.
  
  Move to, per-workspace settings, cloud `workspace_id`, synced folders and Delete are out of scope, as the ticket says.
- **"Default workspace"** is stored in English, as the spec names it. A Spanish UI shows it as written.
- **Residual gap.** The stamp is attached by the preload when a call is made. A timer that survived the remount would carry the new stamp. The switch closes every editor and remounts every page, so I know of no such path, but it is weaker than stamping at the call site.
- **Docs.** The backlog and spec pages live on #431. This PR adds no doc, to avoid a conflict with it.

## Verification

Run in this worktree:

- `node_modules/.bin/vitest run` in `apps/kaipu-record`: 319 files, 3076 tests pass (after merging `main`, including #439). The i18n parity tests pass (22 tests).
- `tsc` for `tsconfig.node.json` and `tsconfig.web.json`: clean.
- `oxlint`: 0 errors. 18 warnings, none in code this PR adds.
- `oxfmt --check .`: clean.

New unit tests:

- `main/workspaces/registry.test.ts`: upgrade; rerun; crash between the writes; corrupt prefs; pending drive; downgrade mirroring and round trip; `workspace.png` and `settings.png` sidecars; add, adopt, copy and relocate; remove.
- `gate.test.ts`: stale workspace and generation rejection, drain, reopen.
- `switch-transaction.test.ts`: order, LOCKED, unavailable, cancel, drain, stale after commit, failed persist.
- Recording writer binding and refusal.
- Legacy cloud ownership.
- Capture binding.
- Toast copy.
- `prepare-switch.test.tsx`: flush, close, Keep editing cancels, Discard proceeds.
- `workspace-switcher.test.tsx`: one workspace and hint, switch, not connected, LOCKED, remount.
- Record page heading.
- Settings → Workspaces.

**Not run:** the Playwright/Electron E2E suite and `/verify`. The owner forbids launching Electron on this machine, so there are no screenshots. Everything visible needs the manual pass below.

## Review round (automated review on `1eb0638`)

All 13 threads are answered in place. Fixed:

- **Switch transaction:** pending captures are dropped only after the switch is persisted; the prepare wait ends for a window that closes or loses its renderer (it used to hold the switch for 120 s); `WorkspaceGate.adopt()` stops a late probe answer from pointing the gate back at the old workspace.
- **Registry:** a failed write rolls back `add`, `remove`, `dismissHint` and `setActive`; updates run one at a time. A probe's own cache update stays best-effort.
- **Editor Save:** the folder is probed before the call enters the gate, so a pending workspace adopting its id can no longer make a save that wrote look stale.
- **Preload:** only a broadcast that changes the stamp (or an abort) clears the switching guard.
- **Media:** every renderer `kaipu-media://` URL goes through `mediaUrl()`, which stamps the workspace; a test blocks hand-built URLs. A URL with no `w` is still served.
- **Switcher and Settings:** a disconnected active workspace shows "Saving to: Paused" and its Finder/Explorer shortcut is disabled; "This PC" on Windows; Escape dismisses the hint only when pressed inside the switcher; a refused Remove shows a toast.
- **Tests:** the test that claimed to cover the `last` refusal is renamed (the branch is unreachable; `registry.ts` now says it is defence in depth).

`main` is merged in (#439 landed). The only conflict was the `LibraryVault` constructor, which is now `(directory, workspaceId, reader)`.

## How to test it yourself

1. **Upgrade an existing library.** Start from a machine with an existing Kaipu library (keep a copy of `~/Library/Application Support/<app>/preferences.json`).
   - Launch this build. The header right of the rail shows "DW · Default workspace | This Mac", with the hint under it.
   - The Library is unchanged.
   - In the library folder, `.kaipu/workspace/identity.json` is the only new file.
   - `preferences.json` has a `workspaces` key and the same `vaultDirectory` as before.
   - Dismiss the hint and relaunch. It does not come back, and the id in `identity.json` is the same.
2. **Add a second workspace.** Open the bar → **Add workspace…** → pick a folder, for example `~/Movies/Personal`.
   - The app switches to it, and the Library is empty.
   - The window title reads "Personal — Kaipu Record".
   - The folder gained only `.kaipu/workspace/identity.json`.
   - The menu now lists "Default workspace" under SWITCH TO, with its item count.
3. **Switch.** Use the bar or the Record page's **Switch**.
   - The Library, tags and the Editor home change with the workspace.
   - With a screenshot editor open with unsaved changes, switching shows the discard dialog. Keep editing cancels the switch; Discard switches.
   - In the video editor, make an edit and switch at once. Switch back and reopen the recording: the edit was saved in its own workspace.
   - A copy-only capture toast that is still showing disappears when you switch.
4. **Unplug a drive.**
   - Add a workspace on a USB drive, make it active, then eject the drive.
   - The bar turns amber: "NOT CONNECTED · CAPTURES PAUSED". Record and Library show "<name> isn't connected".
   - Starting a recording or saving a screenshot shows an error naming the workspace, and nothing is saved in any other workspace.
   - The folder is not recreated on the boot disk.
   - Reconnect the drive and reopen the menu: it is back.
5. **Switch during a recording.**
   - Start a recording and open the bar. A lock icon shows, the menu says "Finish the recording to switch", and every row is disabled.
   - Stop the recording. Switching works, and the take is in the workspace it started in, cursor track included (auto-zoom works in the editor).
   - Repeat during an editor export: "Wait for the export to finish to switch".
6. **Remove from list.**
   - In Settings → Workspaces, choose **Remove from list** on an inactive workspace and confirm. Its folder is untouched.
   - Add the same folder again: it comes back with the same items.
7. **Downgrade.**
   - With Personal active, install 0.15.1. It opens Personal's items.
   - In 0.15.1, change the folder in Settings → Files, then reinstall this build. That folder is now the active workspace, and the old workspaces are still listed.
8. Spanish UI: switch the language and check the switcher, Record heading, toast and Settings → Workspaces copy.
9. **Disconnected drive copy.** With the USB workspace active and the drive ejected, open the bar menu.
   - "Saving to" reads "Paused", not "Here", and the Finder button is greyed out.
   - Reconnect the drive: it reads "Here" and Finder opens the folder.
10. **Close a window mid-switch.** Open a second window (library or editor) and start a switch from the first, with the second showing an unsaved-editor question.
    - Close the second window while the question is open: the switch finishes at once instead of waiting two minutes.
11. **Remove refusal.** In Settings → Workspaces, open Remove on an inactive workspace and leave the dialog open.
    - In the bar, switch to that workspace, then confirm the removal.
    - The dialog closes and a toast explains that the workspace is the active one; the row stays.
12. **Escape.** With the hint still showing, press Escape while a dialog or the screenshot editor has focus: the hint stays. Click "Got it": it goes away for good.
13. **Windows label** (if a Windows machine is at hand): a workspace on the internal drive reads "This PC", not "This Mac".
